You are implementing ONE requirement in the Apache Hadoop source tree at /workspace (a real upstream repo checked out at an earlier state).

REQUIREMENT SLUG: verifyec-debug-tool
REQUIREMENT FILE: /workspace/requirements/verifyec-debug-tool.yaml   <-- READ THIS FIRST

The `title:` field names the real upstream Apache Hadoop JIRA / git commit. Your job is to reproduce that upstream change as faithfully as you can from the requirement text plus the code you find in the tree. Hidden tests derived from the real upstream commit will grade the result, so EXACT naming matters:
  * new/changed configuration keys and their default values (and their entries in *-default.xml)
  * new class / interface / method / field / metric names and their visibility
  * log message wording and format placeholders
  * behavioural details (return values, exception types, ordering, off-by-one boundaries)
If the requirement text names an identifier (class, method, config key, metric, constant), use that identifier verbatim.

HOW TO WORK
1. Read the requirement yaml. Note the JIRA id and the module it belongs to (HDFS / YARN / MAPREDUCE / HADOOP-common / tools).
2. Locate the real code with Grep/Glob. Read enough surrounding code (and the existing tests for it) to make a correct, idiomatic change.
3. Implement the change. Match the surrounding code style, license headers, checkstyle habits (2-space indent, 80-col-ish, final where used, LOG placeholders `{}`).
4. If the change adds a config key, also add it to the matching `*-default.xml` (hdfs-default.xml / core-default.xml / yarn-default.xml / mapred-default.xml) with a sensible description, and to the `DFSConfigKeys`/`YarnConfiguration`/etc. constants class the module uses. Some modules have a TestYarnConfigurationFields / TestHdfsConfigFields style test that requires the xml and the constant to agree - keep them in sync.
5. If the upstream change would have come with tests, add or extend the corresponding test class under the same module (src/test/java/...). Keep tests deterministic and cheap. Do not add tests that need network or a real cluster beyond the usual MiniDFSCluster/MiniYARNCluster idioms already used in that test file.
6. Do NOT run maven/mvn or cmake (there is no warm build environment; it wastes your time). Instead be rigorous by inspection: every symbol you reference must exist (grep to confirm), every new import must be needed and correct, braces/parens balanced, no stale references left behind. Re-read your own final diff (`git diff -- <your files>`) before finishing and fix anything sloppy.
7. Scope discipline: change ONLY what this requirement needs. Do not reformat unrelated lines, do not fix unrelated warnings, do not touch other subsystems. Other agents are concurrently implementing ~380 other requirements in this same working tree.

FORBIDDEN COMMANDS (they would destroy other agents' concurrent work): git checkout / switch / stash / reset / revert / clean / rebase / merge / cherry-pick, `git add -A` or `git add .` without an explicit pathspec, `git commit --amend`, `git rm` of files you did not create, and any `mvn`/`gradle` invocation.

WHEN YOUR IMPLEMENTATION IS COMPLETE - commit it yourself with exactly this shape (substitute the real repo-relative paths you touched, space separated, and keep the flock):

  cd /workspace && flock /tmp/hadoop-git.lock bash -c 'git add -A -- PATH1 PATH2 ... && git diff --cached --binary > requirement_patches/verifyec-debug-tool.diff && git commit -q -m "impl: verifyec-debug-tool" && git log --oneline -1 && wc -c requirement_patches/verifyec-debug-tool.diff'

Rules for that step:
  * List every file you created, modified or deleted as an explicit pathspec. Never a bare directory like `.`.
  * requirement_patches/verifyec-debug-tool.diff MUST come out non-empty (wc -c > 0). If `git commit` reports "nothing to commit", another agent already committed your lines: verify the requirement is genuinely satisfied in the working tree, then report that in your notes.
  * Do not touch requirement_patches/ for any other slug.

FINALLY return ONLY a JSON object (this is your return value, not a message to a human):
{"slug":"verifyec-debug-tool","status":"done"|"partial"|"blocked","files":["..."],"committed":true|false,"patch_bytes":<int>,"summary":"<=3 sentences on what you changed","notes":"anything the orchestrator must know (conflicts, follow-ups, uncertainty)"}

2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Operators troubleshooting erasure-coded files need a direct way to confirm that every block group can actually be reconstructed instead of waiting for later read failures.
6	
7

9	
10	  `hdfs debug verifyEC -file <file>` should inspect each block group of a closed erasure-coded file and report whether reconstruction checks succeed.
11

13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  The command emits per-block-group progress such as `Checking EC block group: blk_...`, returns `Status: OK` for healthy groups, and produces clear failures for missing files, non-files, open files, or files that are not erasure coded.
16

### `zkfc`

Usage: `hdfs zkfc [-formatZK [-force] [-nonInteractive]]`

| COMMAND\_OPTION | Description |
|:---- |:---- |
| `-formatZK` | Format the Zookeeper instance. -force: formats the znode if the znode exists. -nonInteractive: formats the znode aborts if the znode exists, unless -force option is specified. |
| `-h` | Display help |

This command starts a Zookeeper Failover Controller process for use with [HDFS HA with QJM](./HDFSHighAvailabilityWithQJM.html#Administrative_commands).

Debug Commands
--------------

Useful commands to help administrators debug HDFS issues. These commands are for advanced users only.

### `verifyMeta`

Usage: `hdfs debug verifyMeta -meta <metadata-file> [-block <block-file>]`

| COMMAND\_OPTION | Description |
|:---- |:---- |
| `-block` *block-file* | Optional parameter to specify the absolute path for the block file on the local file system of the data node. |
| `-meta` *metadata-file* | Absolute path for the metadata file on the local file system of the data node. |

Verify HDFS metadata and block files. If a block file is specified, we will verify that the checksums in the metadata file match the block file.

### `computeMeta`

Usage: `hdfs debug computeMeta -block <block-file> -out <output-metadata-file>`

| COMMAND\_OPTION | Description |
|:---- |:---- |
| `-block` *block-file* | Absolute path for the block file on the local file system of the data node. |
| `-out` *output-metadata-file* | Absolute path for the output metadata file to store the checksum computation result from the block file. |

Compute HDFS metadata from block files. If a block file is specified, we will compute the checksums from the block file, and save it to the specified output metadata file.

**NOTE**: Use at your own risk! If the block file is corrupt and you overwrite its meta file, it will show up as 'good' in HDFS, but you can't read the data. Only use as a last measure, and when you are 100% certain the block file is good.

### `recoverLease`

Usage: `hdfs debug recoverLease -path <path> [-retries <num-retries>]`

| COMMAND\_OPTION | Description |
|:---- |:---- |
| [`-path` *path*] | HDFS path for which to recover the lease. |
| [`-retries` *num-retries*] | Number of times the client will retry calling recoverLease. The default number of retries is 1. |

Recover the lease on the specified path. The path must reside on an HDFS file system. The default number of retries is 1.

dfsadmin with ViewFsOverloadScheme
----------------------------------

Usage: `hdfs dfsadmin -fs <child fs mount link URI> <dfsadmin command options>`

| COMMAND\_OPTION | Description |
|:---- |:---- |
| `-fs` *child fs mount link URI* | Its a logical mount link path to child file system in ViewFS world. This uri typically formed as src mount link prefixed with fs.defaultFS. Please note, this is not an actual child file system uri, instead its a logical mount link uri pointing to actual child file system|
